name: Get a morning Slack brief on AI news with You.com and Jev

assignments.name: team
assignments.value: A team of developers building AI agents and AI-powered products

assignments.name: caresAbout
assignments.value: ["New AI models they could build with", "New or significantly updated agent frameworks, SDKs, and developer tools", "Laws, rules, or rulings that change what they can ship"]

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'jev-latest', state: { watch: { topic: $json.topic, team: $('Config').first().json.team, cares_about: $('Config').first().json.caresAbout }, article: { title: $json.title, description: $json.description, url: $json.url, published_at: $json.publishedAt } }, questions: {"reports_new_development": {"type": "noul", "instructions": {"question": "Does `article` report a specific development that happened around `article.published_at`?", "focus": "The page itself must report one thing that just happened. Trackers, roundups of many items, explainers, guides, rankings, reference pages, and opinion do not count."}, "criteria": {"true": {"what": "A news report or official announcement of one recent release, launch, law, or ruling", "examples": ["Lab X releases a new open-weights model", "Framework X ships version 2 with a new agent runtime", "Governor signs AI hiring bill into law"]}, "false": {"what": "Evergreen or aggregate content: release trackers, 'AI updates today' or 'this week in AI' roundups, explainers, guides, rankings and listicles, reference pages, or opinion", "examples": ["New AI models: live release tracker", "AI updates today (October)", "Top 7 AI agent frameworks in 2026", "What is an AI agent?"]} } }, "about_topic": {"type": "noul", "instructions": {"question": "Is `article` mainly about `watch.topic`?", "focus": "The topic must be the subject, not a passing mention."} }, "materiality": {"type": "score", "instructions": {"question": "How much should `watch.team` care about `article`, given `watch.cares_about`?", "focus": "Judge whether it changes what the team can build or must do, not how interesting it is."}, "criteria": [{"what": "Noise: commentary, predictions, minor patches, or news with no practical effect", "examples": ["Experts debate whether AI agents are overhyped", "Tool X fixes a typo in its docs"]}, {"what": "Minor: small feature updates, proposals, early-stage bills, or niche releases", "examples": ["Tool X adds a dark mode", "Senator introduces an AI bill"]}, {"what": "Material: a notable model release, a significant new or updated agent framework or tool, a law passed or taking effect, final guidance, or a ruling", "examples": ["Lab X releases a frontier model", "Framework X 2.0 adds multi-agent orchestration", "AI disclosure law takes effect January 1"]}]} } }) }}

parameters.input: ={{ 'Write a short morning brief on ' + $json.topic + ' for ' + $('Config').first().json.team + '. In 1 to 4 bullet points, one per distinct development, say what happened and why it matters. Merge articles that cover the same development, and use product and model names exactly as the articles give them. Today\'s articles: ' + $json.appended_title.map((t, i) => t + ' (' + $json.appended_url[i] + ')').join('; ') }}

assignments.name: text
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const sources = $json.output?.sources ?? []; const body = ($json.output?.content ?? '').replace(/\*\*(.+?)\*\*/g, '*$1*').replace(/^#+\s*(.+)$/gm, '*$1*').replace(/\[\[([\d,\s]+)\]\]/g, (m, n) => n.split(',').map(i => i.trim()).filter(i => sources[i - 1]).map(i => `<${sources[i - 1].url}|[${i}]>`).join('')); const g = $('Group articles by topic').item.json; const meta = g.appended_url.length + ' new ' + (g.appended_url.length === 1 ? 'article' : 'articles') + ' since yesterday'; return ['*' + g.topic + ': morning brief*', '_' + meta + '_', '', body.trim()].join('\n'); })() }}

parameters.content:
## Get a morning Slack brief on AI model, tooling, and policy news with You.com and Jev

Uses the verified You.com node (`@youdotcom-oss/n8n-nodes-youdotcom`), available on n8n Cloud and self-hosted.

Every weekday at 8am, this workflow finds the real AI developments since yesterday and posts one short cited brief per topic to Slack. It's for teams building AI products who want to follow model releases, agent tooling, and AI regulation without reading every newsletter.

### How it works

1. **You.com** searches each topic's news from the past day. Articles seen in earlier runs are skipped.
2. **Jev**, a low-cost classification model from TypeSafe, asks three questions about each article in one call: does it report a real development, is it about the topic, and how much it matters to your team. That costs about $0.00004 per article.
3. Material articles are grouped by topic, so several outlets covering one launch become one bullet.
4. **You.com Research** writes a short brief per topic with linked citations, posted to Slack.

### Requirements

n8n Cloud or self-hosted with the You.com node installed, plus You.com, TypeSafe, and Slack credentials.

### Setup steps

1. Add your **You.com API** credential to both You.com nodes.
2. Add a **Header Auth** credential to the Jev node: name `Authorization`, value `Bearer YOUR_TYPESAFE_KEY`.
3. Connect **Slack** and pick a channel.
4. Edit **Config**: your topics, your team, and what you care about.

### Good to know

A morning costs about $0.01 to $0.04. Topics with no material news get no post. The schedule uses your instance's timezone.

### Customization

Change the topics, or lower `materialityThreshold` for more items.
**Test runs mark articles as seen.** Before your first real run, set this node to *Clear Deduplication History*, execute it once, then switch it back.

## 1. Find the latest news

Search each topic's past day, one article per item, and skip anything seen in earlier runs.

## 2. Judge what matters

Jev scores each article. Only real, material developments pass.

## 3. Brief the team in Slack

Group by topic, then You.com Research writes one short cited brief per topic.
